comment: Third-party clips used as local regression input. The videos themselves are never committed (see .gitignore); this manifest is, so the fixture tree can be rebuilt with tools/video_regression/fetch_youtube.py. 'labelled' entries have an expected rep count in tests/scenarios/youtube.json; 'candidate' entries still need a human rep count before they can assert anything.

clips.label_basis: The uploader's title states 10 reps, and an independent elbow-angle hysteresis count over the clip also gives 10.
clips.notes: Weighted pull-ups, rear view, static camera, full set visible.

clips.label_basis: Independent elbow-angle count and the production engine both give 4.
clips.notes: NASM push-up form demo, side view, static camera.

clips.label_basis: Independent knee-angle count and the production engine both give 2.
Counted by eye from a contact sheet: two shots, one rep each.
clips.notes: Barbell back squat, not an air squat, and there is a hard camera cut at about 5.5s. Kept deliberately: a mid-clip camera change is a case the learned band has to survive.

clips.label_basis: Elbow-angle oracle suggests 11, unverified by eye.
clips.notes: Max pull-up set with heavy wrist dropout (522 of 1916 frames below the confidence floor). Scored 0 before the occlusion fix, 9 now.

clips.label_basis: Oracle gives 28 but with clustered double-counts, so the number is not trustworthy.
clips.notes: Was rejected on 2377 of 2888 frames with 'Get on the bar' — the bar had been mis-established during the walk-up and could never correct itself. Scores 9 since the bar re-establishment fix. Still needs a human rep count before it can assert anything.
Pull-ups with a 5-count hang pause; 1525 nose dropouts. Scored 0 before the occlusion fix, 10 now.

clips.label_basis: Oracle gives 68 with clustered double-counts; not trustworthy.
clips.notes: Long-form push-up tutorial with cuts and talking segments.

clips.label_basis: Oracle gives 6, production gives 5; needs a human count to break the tie.
clips.notes: Squat tutorial with a talking intro before the set.
Full Cindy AMRAP: pull-ups, push-ups and air squats in one clip. Needs per-movement segment labels before it can be scored.

clips.label_basis: One full round: 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, 15 squats, counted by eye from contact sheets and cross-checked against hysteresis on the raw elbow and knee angles; per-rep times in tests/scenarios/cindy.json.
clips.notes: The local fixture is a ~79 s excerpt of a 20-minute AMRAP: one round (pull-ups ~8-23 s, push-ups ~29-52 s, squats ~57-78 s). Production counts only 1 of the 5 pull-ups on this rear three-quarter view, so Cindy mode scores it with setup skipped.

clips.label_basis: Counted by eye from a 2fps contact sheet, then each of the engine's 12 count timestamps was checked against the frame it fired on and every one shows a completed lockout. The boundaries were checked too: the footage fades in at 24.5s with the first full cycle counted at 26.7s, and the athlete holds the top after the last count at 52.1s before the fade-out, so no rep falls outside the counted span.
clips.notes: KNEE push-ups, three-quarter view, static camera, continuous unbroken set. Scored under the standard push-up path and counted 12/12 exactly, with no gate rejection at all during the active portion -- which is the real-footage confirmation of what KneePushupTest asserts synthetically: the push-up path reads the elbow chain and the torso direction, and never looks at the legs, so a knee push-up is the same measurement as a standard one.

Band-assisted pull-ups, front view, single static shot, whole body in frame -- the framing is fine. Scores 0 under pull=band_assisted: 'Get on the bar' rejects 530 of 965 frames and 174 more are lost to 'Show both hands'. The cause is upstream of the counting rules. The bilateral elbow angle swings between -170.9 (a correct dead hang) and -2.7 degrees (anatomically impossible) across the clip, so the wrist and elbow estimates are not stable enough for the bar gate to hold. Front-on framing with a resistance band running down the athlete's centreline is the likely reason. Re-cropping to a 9:16 portrait around the athlete did not help (still 0, 541 'Get on the bar'), so it is not simply subject size. Needs a side-view clip before the assisted rule can be said to have been tested at all.

Band-assisted pull-ups, side view, but an EDITED tutorial: it cuts from a wide shot to a close-up insert around 17-25s and back. Scores 2 under pull=band_assisted, one rep in each continuous segment, with 221 frames of 'Get on the bar' and 386 more with keypoints missing. Unusable as a counting fixture by construction, since a cut moves the bar in frame and crops the body -- the same class of problem already recorded against IODxDxX7oi4. Kept as a candidate only as a record of that.

clips.label_basis: Each of the 5 count timestamps checked against the frame it fired on -- every one is chin-at-bar. Boundaries checked both ways: 4.4-7.0s is a sustained dead hang with no pull, so nothing precedes the first count, and after the fifth at 14.5s he steps out of the band. Independently corroborated by re-running with a hand-measured manual bar, which gives the same five within ~100ms.
clips.notes: Band-assisted pull-ups, front view, band under one knee, single static portrait shot. THE CLIP THAT FOUND THE FALSE-BAR BUG: scored 0 before the fix because the band setup (standing on the box holding the band at chest height, arms straight) satisfied every condition the bar was learned from and fixed it at chest height, after which every rep was refused 'Get on the bar' with no way back. Scores 5/5 once the bar may only be learned with the hands overhead.

clips.label_basis: All 4 count timestamps checked against their frames; every one is a completed top with the chin at the handles. Confidence is medium only because the clip opens mid-set, so the first count's descent happens before the footage starts.
clips.notes: MACHINE-assisted pull-up (kneeling-pad assist machine), rear three-quarter view, static shot. Scored under band_assisted because the app has no MACHINE_ASSISTED variant -- the plan had deferred machine assistance to manual/beta on the grounds that the machine's pads and handles occlude landmarks. This clip is evidence against that caution: the bar gate held on 274 of 301 frames and it counted 4/4. Worth revisiting whether machine-assisted deserves its own AUTO variant.

Band-assisted pull-ups, band behind the athlete with the foot in it, REAR view, single static portrait shot -- framing is fine. Scores 1 under band_assisted, unaffected by the false-bar fix. Limited by the detector rather than the gates: 'Show both hands' rejects 275 of 407 frames, so the wrists are simply not resolved often enough from behind with the arms overhead, and head-above-bar is true on only 7 frames. A rear view with raised arms is the hard case for wrist keypoints; recorded so the next attempt does not re-derive it.

A ten-step pull-up progression in one clip: wall pull-up, high/low/elevated inverted row, scapular pull, chair assisted, negative, jumping, banded, full pull-up. Camera moves between a doorway bar, a hallway and a squat rack, so it is cut footage and cannot be a straight counting fixture -- but it is the best MUST-NOT-COUNT material found so far, because most of the ten movements are not pull-ups. Scores 10 under both strict and band_assisted, at identical timestamps. Verified frame by frame, those ten are: three wall pull-ups (0.50, 3.33, 5.47s, feet bearing weight on the floor), THREE INVERTED ROWS (6.87, 8.53, 9.93s), chair-assisted (13.53s), jumping (16.13s), banded (17.87s) and one full pull-up (18.83s). So only one of the ten counted movements is an unassisted pull-up, and three are horizontal rows. Correctly ignored: the scapular pulls (no elbow flexion, head never crosses the bar) and the negatives (no concentric, and RepCounter books at the top of a climb). THE FINDING: the pull-up path has no body-orientation test. An inverted row passes every gate -- lying or inclined under a bar the wrists are still above the hips, so hangingFromBar holds, the bar is found, the head crosses the bar line and the elbow oscillates a full range. This is the mirror of the push-up path, which does test orientation via upright()/inStartPosition. Discriminating a row from a pull-up needs that same torso-direction test; whether a row is then rejected or counted as its own labelled variant is an open product decision. Expected counts are deliberately not asserted until that is decided. UPDATE after the uprightness gate: strict now counts 7 (was 10) and band_assisted 8 (was 10). The two low inverted rows at 8.53 and 9.93s are gone; the HIGH inverted row at 6.87s still counts, because measured torso verticality on this clip puts it at 0.86-0.98 against 0.92-1.00 for the real vertical pulls -- the distributions overlap, so no threshold separates it honestly. Recorded as the known limit of the orientation signal rather than tuned around.
